Public record of Brazil's Supreme Court · Pet 15.556 and related proceedings · Operation Compliance Zero

The Banco Master case, made navigable.

On 11 September 2026 Brazil's Supreme Federal Court (STF) made 189,000 pages of case records public. This site turns that volume into a map of who appears with whom, in which filing and at what moment, with every relation pointing back to its source. New to Brazil? Start with the primer and the who's who.

        Profiles

        Automatic profiles of everyone with a meaningful presence in the record: at least 8 narrative filings or 4 proceedings. Co-occurrence on the same page does not prove a relationship; each profile says where to check. For curated, human-written bios see the who's who.

        Who's who

        Short bios of the people, companies and institutions a reader needs to hold in mind, written for an audience outside Brazil. Every fact below comes from the public case file as summarised in this site's chronicles, and each card says which filing states it. Allegations are attributed to whoever made them: the Federal Police (PF), the Prosecutor General's Office (PGR), the Central Bank, the reporting justice, or the defence. Nobody described here has been charged, let alone convicted; all of it is investigation-stage material assessed by a judge on a summary basis. If you appear here and see an error, see Disclaimers, item 6. For the automatic, data-driven sheets on all 128 recurring names, see Profiles.

        The bank and the family

        Where the money was raised, and who the police say controlled it.

        Banco Master

        Private bank, São Paulo · formerly Banco Máxima · liquidated 18 November 2025

        A mid-sized bank that, according to the Federal Police summary the reporting justice endorsed on a summary basis, funded itself by selling bank deposit certificates (CDBs) at yields far above the market and poured the money into high-risk operations, illiquid assets and investment funds linked to its own group. The police hypothesis in the Brasília inquiry puts the certificates issued at roughly R$ 50 billion, with about R$ 12 billion possibly uncovered.

        On 18 November 2025 the Central Bank ordered the extrajudicial liquidation of Banco Master and three group companies, appointing a liquidator. The police later estimated the hole the deposit-guarantee fund was covering at close to R$ 40 billion. The ruling of 3 March 2026 describes four alleged cells around the bank: financial, institutional corruption, concealment and laundering, and intimidation.

        Sources: PET 15556 seq 16 pp. 1–2, 23–26; INQ 5026 seq 10 pp. 3750–3751; INQ 5026 seq 12 pp. 10–30. Chronicles: "Seventy-two hours", "Twelve billion and two associations", "The eighteenth of November".

        Open in the graph Search on Google

        Daniel Bueno Vorcaro

        Controlling shareholder of Banco Master · in pre-trial detention since 3 March 2026

        The banker at the centre of the case and the most connected person in this archive: 141 narrative filings across all fifteen proceedings. The record describes him as the bank's controller. A Brasília federal judge first ordered his pre-trial detention on 17 November 2025, in the inquiry about the sale of loan portfolios to the state-owned BRB; he was arrested the next morning as, his defence said, he was about to fly to Dubai to sign the sale of the bank to a consortium. The federal appellate court TRF1 released him on 28 November 2025 under restrictions, including an ankle monitor. In Pet 15.562 the police describe, from the same phone, an "armed wing" paid through his brother-in-law's companies, notes listing the police officers at a closed meeting and the judge's name before the first operation, and a whiteboard headed "TITAN CAYMAN" found in his office; the third-phase searches of 4 March 2026 covered two of his homes.

        On 3 March 2026 Justice André Mendonça ordered his pre-trial detention again, this time on the police allegations concerning the surveillance cell known as "A Turma" and payments to Central Bank supervisors; the ruling transcribes messages attributed to him and states there are "strong indications" that he ordered a staged robbery against a journalist. The Second Panel unanimously confirmed the order. He was moved to the federal penitentiary in Brasília on 5 March 2026, invoked his right to silence before the congressional inquiry committee, and in July 2026 the securities regulator was authorised to question him in prison. No indictment appears in the published record.

        Sources: INQ 5026 seq 10 pp. 3763–3765 and seq 12 pp. 513–535; PET 15556 seq 16 pp. 5–14, 23–26, 40–42, seq 84, seq 294, seq 478; INQ 5026 seq 453. Chronicles: the Pet 15.556 and INQ 5.026 series. PET 15562 seq 1 pp. 3–9, 129–149, seq 54. Chronicles: the Pet 15.562 series.

        Open in the graph Search on Google

        Henrique Moura Vorcaro

        Daniel Vorcaro's father · account of R$ 2.245 billion frozen · detained under another petition

        In the second phase of the operation, on 14 January 2026, the police froze R$ 2,245,235,850.24 in his account at a securities dealer known as REAG; the police representation frames this as money hidden from creditors while the deposit-guarantee fund "bled". His defence answered that the amount is tied up in a private-equity fund backed by carbon credits and has no link to Banco Master; the justice kept the freeze without ruling on the merits. At his home in Belo Horizonte the police seized an Aston Martin, a Bentley, a Range Rover and other cars, watches and iPads; his lawyers, who called him a "peripheral figure" included for family ties, asked for the cars back and were refused in July 2026.

        A procedural order of 6 July 2026 reveals that by then he was in pre-trial detention under a separate petition, Pet 15.978, in connection with "A Turma", an order confirmed by the Second Panel. That petition is not yet covered by the chronicles.

        Sources: PET 15556 seq 16 pp. 23–26, seq 440; PET 15198 seq 21, seq 314, seq 1004, seq 1012 pp. 5–6. Chronicles: "The small hours of 14 January", "The cars", "After the order".

        Open in the graph Search on Google

        Felipe Cançado Vorcaro and Natália Vorcaro

        Daniel Vorcaro's brother and sister · search targets on 14 January 2026

        Both were among the 39 targets of the January 2026 searches. The police link them, with their father, to two holding companies through two real-estate firms. Felipe asked in March 2026 for the release of 21 properties, two vehicles and bank balances, arguing he never took part in the bank's management or ownership and that the two firms never operated and were dissolved in 2022; the request was denied in May 2026. The record says nothing more about Natália's role. Do not confuse Felipe Cançado Vorcaro with "Felipe Mourão", the name used in messages by the alleged coordinator of "A Turma".

        Sources: PET 15198 seq 14 pp. 14–18, seq 21, seq 659. Chronicles: "The fund machine", "The cars".

        Fabiano Campos Zettel

        Described by the police as the group's "financial operator" and Vorcaro's brother-in-law · in pre-trial detention since 3 March 2026

        According to the 3 March 2026 ruling, he handled the payments to the surveillance cell and, through the same structure, the payments to two Central Bank officials; the money left the company Super Participações. The ruling quotes messages such as "today we have to pay Belline's first one". On the night of 13 January 2026 the police told Justice Toffoli he held a ticket to Dubai for 00:50; the justice ordered a temporary detention until seven in the morning so he could not warn relatives before the searches, and the seizure of his passport. Five days after receiving a safe-conduct to appear before the congressional inquiry, he was detained under the March ruling. Requests for a private room for lawyer visits and a television in his cell were denied in July 2026. In Pet 15.562 the police transcribe his "Every month I send it" about the R$ 1 million to Mourão's company and his "Sicário has the names and where to find them?" about the boat captain; at the 4 March 2026 search of his apartment, entered through a broken service door, the police seized a Rolex, a R$ 190,000 necklace and three sheets with screenshots of a Federal Police intelligence system.

        Sources: PET 15556 seq 16 pp. 7–9, 17–22, 32–34, seq 479; PET 15198 seq 85 pp. 1–8, seq 469. Chronicles: "The crew", "The supervisor who reviewed the letter", "The small hours of 14 January". PET 15562 seq 1 pp. 80–83, 111–116, seq 55 pp. 9–12. Chronicles: "Give him a shake", "The sealed boxes".

        Open in the graph Search on Google

        Ana Cláudia Queiroz de Paiva

        Employee of Vorcaro and partner in Super Empreendimentos · alternative measures with ankle monitor

        The ruling reproduces an exchange in which she asks whether a transfer "will be 1 million as usual", is told yes, and sends the receipt to the account indicated by the coordinator of "A Turma". The justice describes her explanation of how a payment avoided going directly from Vorcaro to a Central Bank official as a description of money laundering. She was not detained; she received the package of alternative measures, and a safe-conduct for the congressional inquiry on 13 March 2026. In Pet 15.562 she is described as the person who paid the crew from Super in 2025, including the R$ 1 million entry in the "accounts payable, November 2025" spreadsheet; her lawyers withdrew in May 2026 and a new one appeared in September.

        Sources: PET 15556 seq 16 pp. 11, 21–22, 32–34, seq 196. Chronicles: "The crew", "The supervisor who reviewed the letter". PET 15562 seq 1 pp. 116–119, seq 107, seq 145. Chronicles: "A Turma, the crew", "The sealed boxes".

        Nelson Tanure

        Named by the police as ultimate beneficiary of Lormont Participações and "hidden partner" of Banco Master · search target

        The police representation transcribed by Justice Toffoli names him as the ultimate beneficiary of Lormont Participações, whose notes made up 97% of a receivables fund, and calls him a hidden partner of the bank, asking that his assets be frozen in the same amount as Vorcaro's. The chronicle stresses that "hidden partner" is the police's expression and that, as of publication, the record of that petition holds no answer from him. He was on the list of 39 search targets; on 14 January 2026 the police reported his early flight to Curitiba and obtained a personal search at the Rio airport. The record does not say what, if anything, was seized.

        Sources: PET 15198 seq 14 pp. 14–18, seq 21, seq 85. Chronicles: "The fund machine", "The small hours of 14 January".

        "A Turma": the alleged surveillance cell

        Not to be confused with the Second Panel (Segunda Turma) of the Supreme Court. "A Turma", "the crew", is what the police say the group called itself.

        Luiz Phillipi Machado de Moraes Mourão

        "Felipe Mourão" in the messages · alleged coordinator of "A Turma" · died 6 March 2026

        The ruling describes him as the coordinator of the fourth cell, providing Vorcaro with "sensitive information, monitoring of people and neutralisation of situations considered sensitive", allegedly through improper access to restricted government systems, including, the police say, those of the Federal Police, the federal prosecutors and international bodies. The ruling finds "strong indications" that he received one million reais a month, and transcribes his message about dividing "the monthly" among "the crew". He was detained on 3 March 2026; a firearm found at his arrest led to a separate charge. He died three days later; the circumstances are not in the record. On 29 May 2026 the justice declared the State's power to punish him extinguished, keeping the asset freezes for his heirs and his messages as evidence against others. In Pet 15.562 the police say his crew, "A Turma", looked up sealed cases in the prosecutors' and police systems, sent a forged Interpol document and a forged prosecutor's request to Meta to take down profiles, and was sent after a former boat captain and a chef; they put his receipts since October 2023 at more than R$ 24 million.

        Sources: PET 15556 seq 16 pp. 9–15, seq 58, seq 441 pp. 2–5. Chronicles: "The crew", "After the order". PET 15562 seq 1 pp. 60–120, seq 3 pp. 190–198. Chronicles: "A Turma, the crew", "Give him a shake".

        Open in the graph Search on Google

        Marilson Roseno da Silva

        Retired Federal Police clerk · in pre-trial detention since 3 March 2026

        According to the record he was one of the main operators of the coercion cell, using the experience and contacts of his police career to obtain sensitive data and watch targets, under Mourão's operational lead, in order to "anticipate or neutralise risks" from official investigations, journalists and former employees. In June 2026 the justice refused to unfreeze his accounts but allowed his pension, found to be unrelated to the alleged crimes, to be paid into his wife's account to support her and a minor daughter. The wife and daughter are not named in the record or here. In Pet 15.562 the police say they identified him through a condominium visitor log in Nova Lima on 6 April 2024, and that "A Turma" received R$ 400,000 a month to split among six people, of whom he is the only one identified.

        Sources: PET 15556 seq 16 pp. 14–15, seq 449 pp. 5–7. Chronicles: "The crew", "After the order". PET 15562 seq 1 pp. 60–63, 119–120, 151. Chronicle: "A Turma, the crew".

        Inside the regulator

        Two officials of the department that supervised the bank, and the consultancy through which the police say they were paid.

        Belline Santana

        Head of the Central Bank's bank-supervision department (Desup) · alternative measures, suspended from office

        The ruling states that he provided the bank's controller with strategic advice on its regulatory situation, reviewed drafts of letters the bank would send to the very department he headed, held private meetings with Vorcaro outside the Central Bank's premises and sat in a message group with him and his deputy. According to the police, he received a simulated consultancy contract, through a firm called Varajo, whose stated object was a study on "bringing young people into the financial market" and whose accounts served as a pass-through. The Central Bank had already removed him from his post. No detention was requested; he was barred from entering the Central Bank, had his passport withdrawn and wears an ankle monitor. The evidence was shared with the Central Bank and, in July 2026, with the federal comptroller for a disciplinary and asset inquiry. In Pet 15.504 he is a formal suspect in the police inquiry opened in May 2026; questioned on 25 August 2026, he said he negotiated the contract only with Palhares, never met Zettel, received R$ 3.815 million in total and consulted the Central Bank's internal-affairs office (Corregedoria) informally, without mentioning the amount or Vorcaro's name. In Pet 15.562 two phones and two laptops were seized at his flat on 4 March 2026, with the passwords handed over; on 22 July 2026 the justice allowed a certified copy, provided the defence supplies factory-sealed hard drives with the purchase receipt.

        Sources: PET 15556 seq 16 pp. 6, 17–21, 32–34, 37–38, 42–44, seq 258, seq 480; INQ 5026 seq 12 pp. 528–535; PET 15504 seq 44 pp. 1–2, seq 92 pp. 85–110. Chronicles: "The supervisor who reviewed the letter", "Getting to the other side". PET 15562 seq 105, seq 127, seq 133. Chronicle: "The sealed boxes".

        Open in the graph Search on Google

        Paulo Sérgio Neves de Souza

        Deputy head of Desup at the time · alternative measures, suspended from office

        The ruling describes "direct and frequent" contact with Vorcaro: he sent him the image of his own appointment order, suggested how to behave in a meeting with the Central Bank's president, edited a letter the bank was sending to his own department and warned the bank in advance of transactions flagged by the regulator's monitoring systems. The justice writes that he became "a kind of employee or consultant of Vorcaro for purely private matters". A trip to Orlando for which Vorcaro said he would arrange a guide is listed as a further indication of corruption. He received the same measures as his superior. The congressional inquiry later reported, citing the press, that he was complying with them at a residence in Guaxupé, Minas Gerais. In Pet 15.504 the police add the sale of a farm to a company of Vorcaro's brother-in-law (R$ 4.8 million in the side agreement, R$ 3 million in the deed) and a house sold to another of his companies; questioned on 10 July 2026, he said the messages are ordinary supervision, that his director told him to "hold off" (jogar parado) in September 2024 and that his team drafted 23 liquidation votes. In Pet 15.562 the police note that the Central Bank document the TRF-1 relied on to free Vorcaro, about the 17 November 2025 video call, is signed by him and records that the call was not recorded and no minutes were taken; his own requests for the return of his laptops, one of them needed to answer a tax-authority summons, were declared duplicates of Pet 15.556 on 13 July 2026.

        Sources: PET 15556 seq 16 pp. 5–6, 15–17, 37–38, seq 222, seq 480; PET 15504 seq 2 pp. 45–53, seq 92 pp. 5–36. Chronicles: "The supervisor who reviewed the letter", "Getting to the other side". PET 15562 seq 1 pp. 139–148, seq 7, seq 100, seq 110, seq 129. Chronicles: "Seventeenth of November", "The sealed boxes".

        Leonardo Augusto Furtado Palhares

        Lawyer and company administrator · administrator of Varajo · alternative measures

        "Léo" in the messages. The ruling attributes to him the signing and formalisation of the simulated consultancy proposal, "lending the contract an appearance of legitimacy", and quotes Vorcaro's "see whether Léo can pay, and we reimburse the next day". He received the ankle-monitor package without the Central Bank clause, since he is not a civil servant. Before the congressional inquiry he invoked, besides silence, professional privilege as a lawyer. To the Federal Police, on 15 June 2026, he said the project was requested by Zettel, that the R$ 2 million figure "was suggested" to him, that the money came from Moriah Asset and later from Super, and that the project nonetheless existed. In Pet 15.562 his home was searched on 4 March 2026; as a lawyer he asked for the Bar's safeguards and a mirror copy of his devices, and on 30 March complained that the two dockets had been made available to him "mixed", without page numbers or dates.

        Sources: PET 15556 seq 16 pp. 20–21, 37–38; INQ 5026 seq 639; PET 15504 seq 44 pp. 239–245. Chronicles: "The supervisor who reviewed the letter", "The inquiry becomes a service counter", "We trusted no one". PET 15562 seq 65, seq 86. Chronicle: "The sealed boxes".

        Super Empreendimentos, Moriah Asset, Varajo and the two King companies

        Five companies suspended by court order on 3 March 2026

        The ruling suspended five companies it describes as run by members of the alleged structure and used for fictitious consultancy contracts, group-linked investments, intermediation, simulated asset deals and the payment of illicit expenses, finding "no element pointing to the actual performance of lawful economic activity". Super Empreendimentos e Participações is described as the box from which the transfers to "A Turma" and to the officials left; in the São Paulo petition, a company of the same name receives R$ 650 million at the end of a chain the Central Bank traced through REAG funds. The chronicle notes the record links the two halves of the case through that name without the site asserting they are one. King Participações Imobiliárias is described by the police as Mourão's company.

        Sources: PET 15556 seq 16 pp. 21–22, 33, 38–40; PET 15198 seq 14 pp. 12–14. Chronicles: "The supervisor who reviewed the letter", "The fund machine".

        The Brasília deal: where the operation began

        Inquiry 5.026 concerns the sale of loan portfolios by Banco Master to a state-owned bank. This is the first phase of Operation Compliance Zero, November 2025.

        BRB, Banco de Brasília

        State-owned bank controlled by the government of the Federal District · the buyer

        According to the Central Bank, R$ 12.2 billion flowed from BRB to Banco Master in the first months of 2025: R$ 6.7 billion for loan portfolios and R$ 5.5 billion as a premium; the police count R$ 16.7 billion between July 2024 and October 2025, the source of the "R$ 17 billion" later cited in Congress. The portfolios equalled 30% of BRB's assets. The Central Bank found that BRB assessed the portfolio only after buying it, breached its Basel capital ratio in early 2025 and booked entries without supporting documents; the police say the bank "always wanted to lend money to Banco Master" and could not do so directly because of exposure limits. When the Central Bank asked about the loans' origin, Master first named two civil-servant associations in Bahia and then a company called Tirreno; a Central Bank test of a sample found no matching loans. BRB's president and finance director were removed for 60 days by the November 2025 ruling, which found indications of fraudulent management but a "considerably lower" danger; neither was detained.

        Sources: INQ 5026 seq 10 pp. 3748–3772. Chronicles: "Twelve billion and two associations", "BRB's side", "The eighteenth of November".

        Open in the graph Search on Google

        Tirreno and Cartos

        A shelf company renamed two days before the contract, and the direct-credit company behind it

        Tirreno was created in November 2024 under another name, renamed and recapitalised from R$ 100 to R$ 30 million on 2 December 2024, and signed a partnership contract with Banco Master three days later. The Central Bank found that its only relationship within the financial system was with Master and that it had never made a single payment. The prosecutors speak of "serial forgery of documents"; the judge of "possible document fraud". Its capital was paid in by Henrique Peretto, a partner in Cartos, a licensed direct-credit company that the police say originated the sampled loans and with which Master allegedly "unlawfully associated" to produce and resell non-existent portfolios. Tirreno's director, a former Master employee, and Peretto were held for three days in November 2025.

        Sources: INQ 5026 seq 10 pp. 3750–3765. Chronicles: "Twelve billion and two associations", "The eighteenth of November".

        Tirreno Cartos Google: Tirreno Google: Cartos

        Augusto Ferreira Lima, Luiz Antonio Bull and the other Master directors

        Detained 18 November 2025 · released by TRF1 on 28 November 2025 under restrictions

        The Brasília judge described Augusto Lima as a partner and director of Banco Master who indirectly controlled the two Bahia associations named as the origin of the loans; Luiz Antonio Bull and Ângelo Ribeiro da Silva as the directors who signed the Tirreno contracts and the letter to the Central Bank; and Alberto Felix as a director who signed the partnership contract. All four were released ten days later. Their defences say, respectively, that Lima sold his shares to Vorcaro in May 2024 and never controlled the associations, one of which predates his birth; that Bull, 69, returned home voluntarily to present himself; and that Felix was never a statutory director and signed only to make up a quorum. The chronicle's verdict on the dispute: "who is right, this text does not know."

        Sources: INQ 5026 seq 10 pp. 3763–3765, seq 12 pp. 10–30, 513–538, seq 273. Chronicle: "The eighteenth of November".

        Ibaneis Rocha

        Governor of the Federal District · not a suspect in the petition where he appears

        The governor of the Federal District, whose government is BRB's majority shareholder. He appears in the record only because the congressional inquiry committee summoned him in April 2026, citing his law firm's business with investigated entities and his institutional role in BRB's strategic decisions. Justice Mendonça granted him a safe-conduct, noting that he is not under investigation in that petition and treating him as such only for the purpose of the committee's summons.

        Sources: PET 15556 seq 308. Chronicle: "After the order".

        The São Paulo fund machine

        Petition 15.198 is the second phase, January 2026: an inquiry born in São Paulo that the Supreme Court pulled up to Brasília.

        REAG and João Carlos Falbo Mansur

        Securities dealer group · Mansur described by the Central Bank as its controller · search target

        The Central Bank traced a chain in which Banco Master disbursed R$ 1.45 billion in 2024 and got R$ 1.38 billion back through certificates bought by two REAG funds; a redemption of about R$ 800 million then moved R$ 650 million through a private-equity fund to Super Empreendimentos. A third fund passed from the funds to Vorcaro personally at the end of 2024. The Central Bank reported "doubts as to the real controller". Mansur was added as a target in November 2025 on a Central Bank communication to prosecutors; the declared beneficiaries of the funds are three relatives who are not named here. Henrique Moura Vorcaro's frozen R$ 2.245 billion sat in an account at the group's dealer.

        Sources: PET 15198 seq 14 pp. 12–14, seq 21, seq 512. Chronicles: "From São Paulo to Brasília", "The fund machine".

        Reag Trust Mansur Google: REAG Investimentos Google: João Carlos Mansur

        The single-quotaholder funds and the clinic

        Where the police say the deposit money went

        The prosecutors and police allege that Banco Master directed a large part of the money raised through deposit certificates into receivables funds of which the bank itself was the sole quotaholder, and that of more than R$ 3.5 billion so invested about R$ 1.8 billion bought notes issued by companies tied to the bank's own partners. The emblematic example: Clínica Mais Médicos, a company with zero capital and R$ 54,079.64 in 2023 revenue, issued R$ 361 million in unsecured notes; its president, whom the prosecutors call a front and whom this site does not name, had received emergency welfare payments in 2020 and 2021. Another fund's receivables came from a payment company holding 149.98% of the fund's net worth. The requested freeze totalled R$ 5,775,234,097.25.

        Sources: PET 15198 seq 14 pp. 7–9, 14–18. Chronicle: "The fund machine".

        Clinic in the graph Sefer (ex-Foco DTVM) Search on Google

        Maurício Quadrado and Fernando Alves Vieira

        Search targets · property seized on 14 January 2026 · return refused

        Quadrado is cited by the police as one of the bank's partners and is associated with a securities dealer whose partners issued the notes bought by one fund; with two of them he explained that the issuer existed only to settle labour claims from a Portuguese bank Master had bought, an explanation the police said corroborated their suspicions. Vieira held power of attorney for the clinic's president and is linked by the record to relatives of the bank's partners; at his home the police seized thirteen registered firearms, two vehicles and R$ 184,750 in cash. Both had their requests for restitution denied in May 2026 with the justice's standing formula: seized goods return only when they are "unequivocally" unrelated to the facts. Appeals were pending at publication.

        Sources: PET 15198 seq 14 pp. 14–18, seq 21, seq 660–661. Chronicles: "The fund machine", "The cars".

        The court, the prosecutors, the police and the regulators

        Justice André Mendonça

        Reporting justice of all fifteen proceedings since 13 February 2026

        The most cited name in the archive, 252 narrative filings, because the reporting justice signs everything. He received the case by redistribution in February 2026; the record does not state why. His 48-page ruling of 3 March 2026 ordered four pre-trial detentions, four sets of alternative measures and the suspension of five companies, after refusing the Prosecutor General's request for more time with the words "time flies". The same ruling devotes seven pages to how the arrests should be carried out: discreetly, without handcuffs beyond what a binding precedent allows, with a custody hearing within 24 hours and any release reserved to himself. He also wrote the standing formulas of this record: safe-conducts for everyone summoned by the congressional inquiry, and refusals of every request to return seized cars. On 10 September 2026 he lifted the seal at the request of the Court's presidency.

        Sources: PET 15556 seq 16 (passim), seq 294; PET 15198 seq 403, seq 703, seq 1012. Chronicles: "Seventy-two hours", "What the justice decided, and how", "The new reporting justice and the hundred devices".

        Open in the graph Search on Google

        Justice Dias Toffoli

        Reporting justice until 13 February 2026

        Reporting justice of the constitutional complaint that brought the Brasília inquiry to the Supreme Court in December 2025, and of the São Paulo petition until February 2026. He granted the bank-secrecy lifts and asset freezes on 6 January 2026, the searches against 39 targets on 8 January, and on the night of 13 January, told of a suspect's flight to Dubai, ordered a temporary detention until dawn and rebuked the Federal Police in capital letters for "exclusive inertia" and "express and deliberate disregard" of his order of the previous day. His last act in the Brasília inquiry ordered the full content of seized devices sent to the Court. A four-page order by the Court's president, three pages of them blank, redistributed the case. Two people bearing the Toffoli surname received safe-conducts from his successor for the congressional inquiry; the record does not explain why they were summoned, and this site does not speculate.

        Sources: PET 15198 seq 14, seq 21, seq 85, seq 372; INQ 5026 seq 168, seq 263, seq 366. Chronicles: "From São Paulo to Brasília", "The small hours of 14 January", "The congressman in the drawer".

        The Second Panel

        Five justices · confirmed the 3 March 2026 detentions unanimously

        Under the Court's rules a reporting justice's precautionary orders in criminal matters must be put to a panel. The Second Panel confirmed the March ruling unanimously in a virtual session held between 13 and 20 March 2026; on 31 March the defence's internal appeals were declared moot. The appellate path inside the Supreme Court closed in seventeen days. The same panel confirmed Henrique Moura Vorcaro's detention ordered under Pet 15.978.

        Sources: PET 15556 seq 294 p. 3; PET 15198 seq 1004. Chronicles: "What the justice decided, and how", "The new reporting justice and the hundred devices".

        The Prosecutor General's Office (PGR)

        Paulo Gonet, Prosecutor General · the only body that can bring charges before the Court

        The Prosecutor General opened Petition 15.198 in December 2025 with a one-page request under the highest secrecy grade. In January 2026 his office withdrew the São Paulo police's request to detain Vorcaro, noting he was already under restrictions. In March 2026, given 72 hours to opine on the 164-page police request, it let the deadline lapse and then argued that a deadline "counted in hours" was impossible to meet for measures of such gravity, that there was no imminent danger, and that it could not endorse the requests. The justice ruled anyway. The chronicle's summary: "the body that accuses asks for calm; the judge who decides says calm is a risk." No indictment appears in the published record.

        Sources: PET 15198 seq 1, seq 14 p. 4; PET 15556 seq 16 pp. 2–3, 30. Chronicles: "From São Paulo to Brasília", "Seventy-two hours".

        The Federal Police (PF)

        Investigating body · author of Operation Compliance Zero

        The police wrote the representations that every ruling in this record transcribes: the November 2025 request in Brasília, the São Paulo request that led to the January 2026 searches, and the 164-page request of 27 February 2026 listing seven crime headings, from criminal organisation and money laundering to corruption and obstruction. The Court's relationship with the police was not always smooth: Justice Toffoli's rebuke of January 2026, and Justice Mendonça's February rules confining the case to the assigned officers and sending the forensic examination of about a hundred seized devices back to the police's ordinary flow.

        Sources: PET 15556 seq 1, seq 16; PET 15198 seq 85, seq 403. Chronicles: "Seventy-two hours", "The small hours of 14 January", "The new reporting justice and the hundred devices".

        The Central Bank of Brazil

        Supervisor of the banks · liquidated the Master group on 18 November 2025

        The regulator whose March 2025 letter to Banco Master, asking about the loans sold to BRB, started the Brasília inquiry, and whose reports on BRB's prudential breaches and on the REAG chain are transcribed throughout the record. On the afternoon of 17 November 2025 its supervisors held a video call with Vorcaro in which, according to a Central Bank document, he said he would fly to Dubai that day to sign the bank's sale; the next day it decreed the liquidation. Two of the officials on that call are among the suspects. Its two most recent presidents appear only because Congress summoned them: Justice Mendonça found "no indication whatsoever" of the former president's involvement, the only such statement about anyone in the whole series of rulings, and converted the summons into an invitation.

        Sources: INQ 5026 seq 10 pp. 3750–3762, seq 12 pp. 528–535, seq 423; PET 15198 seq 14 pp. 12–14. Chronicles: the INQ 5.026 series, "The supervisor who reviewed the letter".

        CVM, CGU, FGC and the congressional inquiry

        The securities regulator, the federal comptroller, the deposit-guarantee fund, and Congress

        The securities regulator (CVM) had already sanctioned Banco Master on at least five earlier occasions, filed a criminal complaint in June 2025 and, in July 2026, was authorised to question Vorcaro in prison in three administrative investigations. The federal comptroller (CGU) obtained the evidence against the two Central Bank officials for a disciplinary and asset inquiry. The deposit-guarantee fund (FGC) is the entity the police say was "bleeding" to cover the bank's hole. The joint congressional inquiry into organised crime summoned most of the suspects, the governor, the former Central Bank president and the two Toffolis; the Court answered each summons with a safe-conduct, and several of them, Vorcaro included, invoked their right to silence.

        Sources: PET 15556 seq 16 pp. 23–26, seq 478, seq 480; PET 15198 seq 14 pp. 7–9; INQ 5026 seq 423, seq 453. Chronicles: "After the order", "The inquiry becomes a service counter".

        Not yet covered. Petitions 15.976, 15.977, 15.978 and 16.019 form a cluster with their own cast, among them the most cited names in those dockets, which the chronicles have not yet read. The constitutional complaint RCL 88.121, Inquiry 5.035 and Petitions 15.478, 15.504 and 15.562 have their own series, each with an English edition. Bios are added and extended as each series is written. The "Search on Google" buttons open a web search for the name; what you find there is not part of this record.

        Brazil primer: the court, the cops, the regulators and the jargon

        What a reader outside Brazil needs in order to follow this record. General background on how Brazilian institutions work; where the text refers to this case, it says only what the case file itself says. Portuguese terms are kept in italics because they recur on every page of the record.

        1. Why a bank case sits at the Supreme Court

        Brazil's Supremo Tribunal Federal (STF, Supreme Federal Court) is both the constitutional court and the trial court for a short list of officials who hold what Brazilians call foro por prerrogativa de função, a privileged venue: sitting members of Congress, cabinet ministers and a few others can only be investigated and tried by the STF. When such a person surfaces in an investigation, the whole case, or the part touching that person, moves up to the Court. The Court can also pull a case up through a reclamação (RCL), a constitutional complaint asserting that a lower court is trespassing on the STF's jurisdiction. Both mechanisms appear in this record.

        The Court has eleven justices, called ministros in Portuguese, appointed by the President with Senate approval and serving until the age of 75. It sits as a full bench (Plenário) or as two panels of five, the Primeira and Segunda Turma. Every case is assigned by lot to one justice, the relator, translated here as reporting justice. The relator runs the case day to day and can decide urgent measures alone, in a single-justice ruling (decisão monocrática). Such rulings are then put to the panel, which either confirms or overturns them; the record calls that confirmation a referendo. A change of relator by redistribution happened in this case, and both panels' names appear in the filings.

        2. The three kinds of proceeding in this record

        INQ, inquérito
        A criminal investigation supervised by the Court. The Federal Police investigates; the reporting justice authorises intrusive measures; the Prosecutor General decides whether to indict. An inquiry is not a charge: nobody in an INQ has been accused of anything by a prosecutor yet.
        PET, petição
        An ancillary or precautionary proceeding. In the STF's practice, requests for searches, detentions, asset freezes and similar measures are docketed as separate petitions attached to an inquiry. That is why the "main" proceeding here, Pet 15.556, is technically a petition and not the inquiry itself. Pet 15.198 is the docket where the second phase of the operation was requested and decided.
        RCL, reclamação
        A constitutional complaint. Used here to bring a São Paulo investigation up to the STF on the argument that it touched the Court's exclusive jurisdiction.

        Brazilian docket numbers use a dot as a thousands separator: "Pet 15.556" is petition number fifteen thousand five hundred and fifty-six. This site writes the same number as "PET 15556". Inside each proceeding, every docket entry carries a sequence number, seq, which is also the beginning of the file name in the STF's public package; the "Where to check" tables on this site cite proceeding, seq and page.

        3. Who does what

        Polícia Federal (PF), the Federal Police
        Investigates federal crimes, including crimes against the financial system and money laundering. Under Brazilian procedure the police cannot search, detain or freeze assets on their own authority outside a crime in progress: they file a representação, an application, and a judge decides. A delegado is a police chief with a law degree who signs those applications. "Operação Compliance Zero" is the PF's name for this investigation.
        Procuradoria-Geral da República (PGR), the Prosecutor General's Office
        The head of the federal prosecution service, the Ministério Público Federal. Before the STF, only the PGR can bring charges. Before deciding a police request, the reporting justice normally gives the PGR vista, a referral for an opinion within a deadline. A PGR manifestação is that opinion; a denúncia would be an indictment, which is a later stage than anything summarised on this site.
        The defence
        Lawyers are identified in the record by their bar registration (OAB). They file petições asking, for instance, for the return of seized property or the revocation of detention. Their filings are part of the archive, but the precautionary rulings summarised here were, as a rule, issued before the defence was heard.
        Banco Central do Brasil (BCB), the Central Bank
        Licenses and supervises banks. Its bank-supervision department appears in the record under the acronym Desup. When a bank is judged unrecoverable, the Central Bank can order its liquidação extrajudicial, an extrajudicial liquidation: the bank is closed and wound up by a liquidator appointed by the Central Bank, outside the courts. Two other units of the Central Bank appear in Pet 15.504: its legal department, the Procuradoria-Geral do Banco Central (PGBC), an in-house counsel's office that is not a prosecution service; and its internal-affairs office, the Corregedoria-Geral (Coger), which opens disciplinary inquiries into the Central Bank's own staff, including the sindicância patrimonial, an asset inquiry into whether a civil servant's wealth matches their income. A termo de comparecimento and an ofício are the supervisor's two written instruments for telling a bank to fix something; the first summons the bank's controller to commit to a plan, the second is a letter.
        Fundo Garantidor de Créditos (FGC)
        The private deposit-guarantee fund financed by the banks themselves. It repays depositors and holders of bank deposit certificates up to a per-person, per-institution ceiling when a bank is liquidated. Because of it, high-yield bank paper sold to retail investors through brokerage platforms carries an implicit safety net, which is part of the background the record describes.
        Comissão de Valores Mobiliários (CVM)
        The securities regulator, Brazil's counterpart to the SEC. Supervises investment funds, asset managers and public companies.
        Controladoria-Geral da União (CGU)
        The federal government's internal-control and anti-corruption agency. Among other things it runs disciplinary proceedings against federal civil servants, which is the capacity in which it appears here.
        Tribunais Regionais Federais (TRF)
        The federal appellate courts. TRF1 sits in Brasília and covers the Federal District and much of the centre and north; TRF3 sits in São Paulo. A Vara Criminal Federal is a first-instance federal criminal court; the record includes a copy of a criminal action from the 6th Federal Criminal Court of São Paulo.
        CPMI, Comissão Parlamentar Mista de Inquérito
        A joint congressional inquiry committee, with power to summon witnesses. When a person under investigation is summoned, the Court may issue a salvo-conduto, a safe-conduct order guaranteeing that the person may remain silent and will not be arrested for doing so.

        4. The measures a judge can order before any trial

        Busca e apreensão, search and seizure
        A warrant to search premises and seize documents, devices, cash and vehicles. Seized property is inventoried and can be released back on request (restituição de coisas apreendidas).
        Prisão temporária, temporary detention
        A fixed-term detention, requested by the police during an investigation, to secure evidence or prevent flight. It expires on its own unless extended.
        Prisão preventiva, pre-trial detention
        Open-ended detention that the judge must justify under article 312 of the Code of Criminal Procedure: evidence that a crime occurred and indications of authorship (fumus commissi delicti), plus a concrete danger created by the person's liberty (periculum libertatis), for one of the purposes the article lists: protecting public order or economic order, the convenience of the investigation (conveniência da instrução criminal), or ensuring that the criminal law can be enforced. The judge must also explain why less severe alternatives would not do. The ruling summarised in the Pet 15.556 chronicles works through exactly those steps.
        Medidas cautelares diversas, alternatives to detention
        Electronic ankle monitor (tornozeleira eletrônica), surrender of passport, ban on contact with other suspects, suspension from a job or from company management.
        Sequestro, bloqueio, asset freeze
        Freezing of bank accounts, funds or property up to an amount the judge sets, so that they are available for eventual forfeiture or compensation.
        Cognição sumária, summary assessment
        The standard for all of the above: the judge decides on the probability of the allegations, on the file as it stands and usually without hearing the defence. It is not a finding of guilt, and Brazil's Constitution (article 5, LVII) presumes innocence until a conviction becomes final.
        Sigilo, sealing
        Investigations run under seal. The seal can be lifted in whole or in part by the reporting justice; that is what happened on 10 September 2026, and the resulting public package is the sole source of this site. Even after unsealing, the STF's case headers still read "under seal", so this site rebuilt the list of parties from the body of the filings.

        5. The financial instruments that keep coming up

        CDB, Certificado de Depósito Bancário
        A bank-issued time deposit, the basic retail funding instrument of a Brazilian bank, covered by the FGC guarantee and widely sold through investment platforms.
        FIDC, Fundo de Investimento em Direitos Creditórios
        A receivables fund: a vehicle that buys loans, invoices or other credit rights. Its shares are called quotas; a fund with a cotista único has a single quotaholder, which is the kind of structure the police filings describe at length.
        FIP, Fundo de Investimento em Participações
        A private-equity fund that holds stakes in companies.
        DTVM, Distribuidora de Títulos e Valores Mobiliários
        A securities distributor, a kind of broker-dealer licensed by the Central Bank and the CVM. A DTVM often acts as the administrator of investment funds, the entity legally responsible for the fund, while a separate gestora (asset manager) makes the investment decisions.
        CNPJ and CPF
        The company registry number and the individual taxpayer number. Every Brazilian company and every person has one; the record is full of them. This site publishes company numbers and never publishes individual ones.
        Money
        Amounts are in Brazilian reais (R$). Over 2025 and 2026 one US dollar bought roughly five to six reais; check the rate of the day before converting a figure. Brazilian usage writes R$ 1.000.000,00 for one million.

        6. How to read a Brazilian court filing

        • Parties and companies are written in CAPITAL LETTERS; that convention is what this site's name extraction relies on.
        • A single-justice ruling opens with a summary of the request (relatório), then the reasoning (fundamentação), then the operative part (dispositivo). The chronicles on Pet 15.556 follow that anatomy.
        • Dates are day/month/year. "3.3.2026" is 3 March 2026.
        • "Ministro" before a name means a Supreme Court justice, not a member of the cabinet. "Desembargador" is an appellate judge; "juiz" a first-instance judge; "delegado" a police chief. "Procurador" needs care: a procurador da República is a federal prosecutor, but the Procurador-Geral do Banco Central is the Central Bank's general counsel, a government lawyer, not a prosecutor.
        • Nothing in the record summarised here is a conviction. Every allegation belongs to whoever made it, and this site keeps that attribution: "the PF states", "the PGR argues", "the ruling says".

          Chronicles · reading, not filtering

          The case told to those who will not read 189,000 pages

          Opinion pieces by the project's author, written on the same public data as the site. Light in tone, checkable in fact: every number points to the archive and every name to a profile. They are not news, not an expert report, and they assert nobody's guilt. Every chronicle is available in full in English. The English editions are translations of the Portuguese originals, which remain the reference text.

          Subscribe via the RSS feed (feed in Portuguese; every chronicle opens here in English). Factual errors: open an issue in the repository; the rule is to fix fast and leave a record.

          How this was made

          Source

          The STF published the case records on 11 September 2026 (press note, in Portuguese). The package holds 4,258 PDFs and 49 videos. Only the text was used. Neither the package nor the documents are on this site.

          Pipeline

          1. Manifest and text. SHA-256 hash and metadata for every file; page-by-page text extraction. Pages without a text layer (1.8%) went through Portuguese OCR.
          2. Structured extraction. Regular expressions for case numbers, corporate tax IDs (CNPJ), dates, references to other proceedings and names in capital letters, which is how Brazilian legal filings write the parties.
          3. Roles. Company (corporate suffix or term), official (public office in context, or a signature on every page of a long filing), lawyer (sender of the e-filing receipt, or a bar registration next to the name), person (everyone else). A manual curation layer corrects roles, merges spelling variants and discards fragments that are not names.
          4. Relations. Two entities are linked when they appear on the same page of a narrative filing. Exhibits such as bank statements, tables, powers of attorney and identity documents are left out, because they mass-produce spurious relations. The weight is the number of distinct filings in common.
          5. Network metrics (v0.2). Bridges is betweenness centrality: how many shortest paths between other pairs run through the node, with distance equal to the inverse of the weight. Influence is weighted PageRank. Clustering is the clustering coefficient (how much a node's neighbours link to one another). Outside the cluster is the share of link weight that leaves the node's community (Louvain communities). Specificity of a link is the lift: observed filings in common divided by those expected if the two names appeared independently; the site combines lift and volume to rank pairs. In the graph and in the analysis, bridges and influence are recomputed on the visible slice, because lawyers and officials who sign many filings distort the global computation.
          6. Sanitization. See the policy (Portuguese). In short: public entities and people named in judicial acts appear by name; incidental people become pseudonyms; personal data stays out.

          Limits, plainly

          • Co-occurrence on the same page is not a proven relationship. It is an invitation to read the filing.
          • Namesakes exist and may have been merged. Spelling variants of the same name were merged by a simple rule and by curation.
          • OCR makes mistakes; truncated names or swapped letters may appear.
          • Monetary amounts were not published: automatic extraction from bank statements is unreliable.

          How to check

          Every citation gives the proceeding, the filing's sequence number and the page. Download the STF package from the link in the press note, open the proceeding's folder and the file whose name begins with that sequence number.

          Chronicles

          The Chronicles section is editorial: opinion pieces by the project's author, written on top of the same public, sanitized data. They live in docs/posts/, in Markdown, with date and sources; the English edition of each one lives in docs/posts/en/. The database (graph, profiles, analysis) does not depend on them and does not change because of them. When a chronicle cites a number, the number comes from docs/data/; when it cites a filing, it gives proceeding, seq and page.

          English edition

          This page is generated from the Portuguese original by pipeline/build_en.py, which translates the interface and the static text by exact-string substitution and fails when the original changes without a matching translation. The who's who and the primer are written in English only and draw solely on facts stated in the public record and summarised in the chronicles. Every chronicle is translated in full, paragraph by paragraph, from the Portuguese original, which remains the reference text. Legal terms are rendered in standard English with the Portuguese term alongside where the English is only an approximation.

          Disclaimers, limits and rights

          Everything this site asks you to know before using what it shows, gathered in one place. The same notices appear scattered across the other sections; here they are in full.

          1. What this site is

          • A personal, independent civic project. It is not affiliated with the Supreme Federal Court, the Federal Police, the Public Prosecutor's Office, the Central Bank, or any party, suspect, lawyer or media outlet involved in the proceedings.
          • A navigable index of public documents: the case records the STF made public on 11 September 2026 (Petition 15.556 and fourteen related proceedings). The primary source is the STF press note and the package it links to. The site does not host the documents.
          • A work under review (version 0.2). Extraction of names, roles and relations is automatic and may contain errors. Everything may change between versions; the change history is public in the repository.

          2. What this site is not

          • It is not evidence of anything. Appearing in the graph, in a profile or in a chronicle does not mean involvement in a crime. Co-occurrence on the same page of a court filing is a reading cue, not a proven relationship.
          • It is not a conclusion about guilt. Everyone mentioned is entitled to the presumption of innocence (Brazilian Constitution, art. 5, LVII). The precautionary rulings described here are issued on a summary assessment (cognição sumária), before any trial, and the defence, as a rule, had not yet been heard in the filings summarised.
          • It is not news or reporting. No information was gathered outside the record. What the record says is attributed to whoever said it (police, prosecutors, judge, defence).
          • It is not legal, financial or investment advice. Do not use this site to decide on contracts, investments, hiring or reputations.
          • It is not a complete database. Only the text of the filings was used; the 49 videos in the package were left out. Exhibits (bank statements, tables, powers of attorney, identity documents) do not feed the graph.

          3. Names, personal data and sanitization

          • Appear by name: companies and entities; officials acting in their capacity; lawyers acting in the record; people named in a ruling, procedural order or initial petition; people recurring in two or more proceedings and three or more filings. The full rule is in the sanitization policy (Portuguese).
          • All other natural persons appear as a stable code ("Pessoa A1B2C3"), generated with a salt that is not in the repository.
          • Never published: taxpayer numbers (CPF), ID numbers, bar registrations, addresses, phone numbers, e-mails, bank accounts, Pix keys, file names, passages of full text, any content of filings classified as identity documents, monetary amounts extracted automatically from bank statements.
          • The only data outlet to the site is an export script that fails if it detects forbidden patterns. The report of that check is kept outside the repository.
          • Namesakes may have been merged; spelling variants may have been split; OCR (1.8% of pages) swaps letters. If you spot an error, see item 6.

          4. Chronicles, who's who and primer

          • The Chronicles section is editorial: opinion pieces by the project's author, written on the same public filings. They have a literary tone; they involve no outside reporting. They are written in Portuguese and every one is translated in full into English; the original remains the reference text.
          • Every statement of fact names who made it in the record and ends with the proceeding, the filing's sequence number and the page. When the text opines, it is opining; when it describes, it describes what is written in the filing.
          • The chronicles follow the same naming policy as the database: they do not name people the database pseudonymizes, nor people the ruling itself shields (journalists, employees, incidental relatives).
          • The English who's who and primer follow the same rules: every fact is attributed to the filing that states it, allegations are presented as allegations, and nobody is described as guilty.
          • Factual errors in chronicles, bios or the primer are corrected in the text, with a visible correction note and a record in the repository history.

          5. Metrics and analysis

          • Bridges (betweenness), influence (PageRank), clustering, clusters (Louvain) and specificity (lift) are mathematical measures of name co-occurrence on pages. They describe the structure of the text of the record, not the reality of the facts. A name with many "bridges" is a name that appears on pages of different groups; nothing more.
          • The timeline dates are dates cited in the filings, not dates of events.
          • Definitions and limits: the Method section and METODOLOGIA.md (Portuguese).

          6. If you appear here

          • You may request a review of identification (namesake, wrong name), of role (person, company, official, lawyer), of visibility (an incidental mention that should be pseudonymized) or of any statement in a chronicle or bio.
          • Channel: open an issue in the repository. You need not identify yourself beyond what is necessary to point out the error; do not send personal documents. The commitment is to answer and, where there is an error, to correct it with a public record of the correction.
          • The site processes only data extracted from public acts, for informational and public-interest purposes, and keeps to the minimisation above. Requests concerning personal data are received through the same channel.

          7. Privacy of the site's visitors

          • The site is static, hosted on GitHub Pages. There are no accounts, forms, first-party cookies, analytics or tracking. None of your data is sent to the project's author.
          • Your browser stores locally, and only there, usage preferences: light/dark theme, tour step, computed graph layout. Clearing the site's data erases everything.
          • When the page loads, the browser fetches fonts from Google Fonts and code libraries from jsDelivr, in addition to the GitHub Pages files. Those services receive, as any server does, the visitor's IP address, and have their own policies.

          8. Licences and reproduction

          • Code: MIT. Derived data in docs/data/: Creative Commons BY 4.0 (cite "autos-abertos" and the version). Chronicles, bios and primer: the author's text; reproduction allowed with attribution and link, without altering the meaning.
          • The original documents are public acts of the STF and follow the Court's terms of use. Cite them by their source, not by this site.
          • Anyone reproducing data or text from here takes on the same limits: nothing here authorises asserting anyone's guilt.

          9. Security and integrity

          • The public repository contains only code, sanitized data and texts. The raw archive, full text, manifests, pseudonymization salts and curation files stay out, by rule of the .gitignore and of the export gate.
          • The repository has automatic secret scanning and protection against history rewriting. Vulnerabilities or leaks: report through the repository's security tab or by issue, without publishing the exposed data.
          • Data version and generation date: footer of the Method section.
